title: Legacy CRM Validation Framework — OQ/PQ Test Script Architecture for Regulated Environments
summary: The formal validation qualification framework for a legacy life sciences CRM in regulated pharma environments, covering the structural architecture of Operational Qualification (OQ) and Performance Qualification (PQ) test scripts, the document control and evidence chain, and the regulatory traceability model linking every test step to specific CFR requirements.

findings.qualification_tiers: The validation framework uses two qualification tiers: Operational Qualification (OQ) verifies that the system functions correctly under normal and edge-case conditions across all features. Performance Qualification (PQ) verifies that the system produces expected results under real-world production conditions with representative data volumes. OQ scripts are more numerous and granular (60+ scripts per release), covering every functional area. PQ scripts are focused on end-to-end workflows that prove production readiness (5 scripts per release). Both tiers are versioned and re-executed with each major platform release.
findings.test_script_document_structure: Each test script follows a standardized document structure: (1) Pre-Execution signature block — author name and title, tester names with titles, signatures, initials, and dates in dd-mmm-yyyy format; discrepancy count; test sheet run number; overall pass/fail status. (2) Computer Specifications — device type (iPad, Laptop/Computer), software version (platform release identifier), OS version, and URL endpoint. (3) Test Case Description — narrative statement of what the script validates. (4) Requirements Tested — enumerated list of specific CFR citations. (5) Test Sheet Dependency — prerequisite scripts that must execute first. (6) Pretest Setup — environmental preparation steps with fill-in fields for test data (representative names, login credentials, product/lot numbers, inventory quantities). (7) Numbered step-by-step Instructions with Expected Results, Documented Evidence flag (Y/N), Actual Result field, Pass/Fail field, and Initials/Date field per step. (8) Post-Execution signature block — approver name, title, signature, and date.
findings.regulatory_traceability: Every test script maps to specific 21 CFR Part 11 and 21 CFR Part 203 requirements. Part 11 covers electronic records and signatures: 11.10(a) system validation, 11.10(e) signer authentication, 11.10(f) operational system checks, 11.10(h) device checks, 11.50(a)(1-3) electronic signature manifestation, 11.50(b) name and date display, 11.70 signature/record linking. Part 203 covers sample distribution: 203.31(a-d) sample distribution records, 203.31(b)(1)(i-vi) required distribution data elements, 203.38(a-b) sample receipt and storage, 203.60(a)(2)(i-ii) reporting requirements. Scripts explicitly enumerate which CFR citations they satisfy, creating a traceable compliance matrix.
findings.documented_evidence_chain: Steps flagged with DE=Y (Documented Evidence) require the tester to capture a screen printout, physically attach it to the test sheet, and label, initial, date, and paginate the printout. This creates a physical evidence chain that auditors can inspect. The evidence chain is critical for regulatory submissions — it proves the system was actually tested, not just documented. Steps flagged DE=N require only pass/fail attestation in the Actual Result column with tester initials and date.

title: Legacy CRM OQ Coverage Map — Offline, Online, and Ohio TDDD Compliance Scenarios
summary: The complete operational qualification test coverage matrix for a legacy life sciences CRM, organized across offline (iPad), online (web), and state-specific controlled substance compliance scenarios, with the Ohio Terminal Distributor of Dangerous Drugs (TDDD) framework as the reference compliance model.

findings.offline_oq_coverage: 27 scripts covering iPad-based offline functionality. Category 1 (Access): application login including biometric authentication (Touch ID). Category 2 (Calls and Sampling): new call with detail and sample using signature capture, new call with document ID verification, Direct-to-Physician (DTP) disbursement with both signature and document ID variants, DTP with controlled substance variants (signature and document ID). Category 3 (Group Calls): group call recording for healthcare organizations on web, editing and deleting sample calls on web. Category 4 (Ohio TDDD Offline): 15 scripts covering all permutations of controlled substance schedules (C2, C2 LIMITED, C3, C3 LIMITED, EXEMPT) crossed with verification methods (signature vs document ID) and disbursement types (standard vs DTP). Category 5 (Attendee Sampling): multi-attendee sampling scenarios where samples are disbursed to individual attendees within a group interaction.
findings.online_oq_coverage: 31 scripts covering web-based online functionality. Category 1 (Access): web application login. Category 2 (Inventory): receive shipment with initial inventory setup, ad hoc inventory creation, periodic inventory reconciliation, audited inventory verification. Category 3 (Calls and Sampling): call with detail and sample using document ID, group call for healthcare organizations, DTP with document ID, DTP with controlled substance. Category 4 (Inventory Transfers): acknowledgment of shipment (manual), transfer in (manual), transfer out, return, adjustments. Category 5 (Data and Compliance): data retention with signature view, attendee-level sampling for multiple attendees, call unlock for submitted calls. Category 6 (Ohio TDDD Online): 10 scripts covering controlled substance schedules (C2, C2 LIMITED, C3, C3 LIMITED, EXEMPT) with document ID verification for standard and DTP disbursements. Category 7-8 (Call Management): editing and deleting sample calls for both standard users and admin users. Category 9 (License Validation): state license validation for inactive and revoked licenses.
findings.pq_coverage: 5 scripts covering end-to-end production qualification. Offline PQ: new call workflow (complete call lifecycle from creation through submission), DTP with document ID (physician-directed disbursement end-to-end). Online PQ: acknowledgment of shipment (inventory receipt lifecycle), return (sample return workflow), periodic inventory (reconciliation lifecycle). PQ scripts use the same document structure as OQ but focus on proving that a complete business workflow executes correctly rather than testing individual feature functions.
findings.ohio_tddd_compliance_model: Ohio Terminal Distributor of Dangerous Drugs compliance is the most granular testing area, with 25 scripts (15 offline + 10 online) covering every permutation of: (1) Controlled substance schedule — C2 (Schedule II, highest restriction), C2 LIMITED, C3 (Schedule III), C3 LIMITED, and EXEMPT (exempt preparations). (2) Verification method — electronic signature capture (offline only) vs document ID verification (both offline and online). (3) Disbursement type — standard HCP disbursement vs DTP (Direct-to-Physician) disbursement. This matrix ensures that the CRM correctly enforces the different documentation and tracking requirements for each substance schedule and distribution method under Ohio state regulations.
findings.platform_parity_testing: The test suite explicitly validates both offline (iPad native application) and online (web application via Chrome) execution modes. The same functional scenarios are tested in both modes where applicable, ensuring feature parity between offline and online. Device specifications are recorded per script — iPad for offline scripts (with OS version), laptop/computer for online scripts (with Chrome version and Salesforce instance URL). This dual-mode testing is critical because the offline application stores and processes data locally before synchronization, while the online application operates directly against the server.

title: Legacy CRM Sample Compliance Testing — Inventory Lifecycle and CFR 203 Distribution Controls
summary: The sample management compliance testing methodology for a legacy life sciences CRM, covering the complete inventory lifecycle from shipment receipt through periodic reconciliation, the sample disbursement controls enforced by 21 CFR Part 203, and the signature and document ID verification workflows that ensure regulatory chain of custody.

findings.inventory_lifecycle_testing: Five inventory operation types are validated through dedicated OQ scripts: (1) Receive Shipment with Initial Inventory — verifies that a new representative can acknowledge a home office shipment, confirms the beginning inventory is established, and validates that initial inventory can only be created once. Tested with 7 line items across multiple product families and lot numbers. (2) Ad Hoc Inventory — verifies on-demand inventory snapshots outside the periodic cycle. (3) Periodic Inventory — verifies scheduled inventory reconciliation with opening balance, quantity out, and system count validation per product and lot. (4) Audited Inventory — verifies formal audit-grade inventory counts with enhanced documentation. (5) Transfer operations — transfer in, transfer out, and return workflows for inter-representative and return-to-warehouse sample movements.
findings.sample_disbursement_controls: Sample disbursement calls require: lot number selection from the representative's current inventory, quantity entry with validation against available stock, healthcare provider state license validation (calls blocked for inactive or revoked licenses), and either electronic signature capture or document ID verification. The system enforces that disbursement cannot occur to a location with an invalid state license — this is tested with dedicated scripts (OQ 9.0, 9.1) that verify the system blocks sampling when a license is inactive or revoked. After disbursement, the system automatically updates the representative's inventory balance.
findings.signature_vs_document_id_verification: Two parallel verification methods exist for sample receipt: (1) Electronic Signature — the healthcare provider signs on the device screen, the signature is captured and stored as part of the call record. Tested extensively in offline OQ scripts where the iPad captures signatures natively. The signature satisfies 21 CFR Part 11 requirements for electronic signatures (11.50, 11.70). (2) Document ID — a pre-printed document identification number is recorded as an alternative to electronic signature, used when a provider has already signed a physical receipt form. Both methods satisfy 21 CFR Part 203 documentation requirements for sample distribution records.
findings.controlled_substance_additional_controls: Controlled substance disbursements add requirements beyond standard sample distribution: state-specific reporting obligations (Ohio TDDD being the most comprehensive model tested), substance schedule classification affecting the documentation threshold and tracking granularity, and dedicated test scripts that validate the system correctly differentiates handling between C2, C3, LIMITED, and EXEMPT classifications. DTP (Direct-to-Physician) controlled substance disbursements follow a distinct workflow where samples are shipped directly to the physician's office rather than hand-delivered, requiring additional chain-of-custody documentation.
findings.data_retention_and_audit_trail: Data retention scripts verify that historical sample transactions, signatures, and call records remain accessible and viewable after submission. The audit trail captures the complete lifecycle: who disbursed what product, in what quantity, from which lot, to which provider, at which location, with which verification method, at what timestamp. This audit trail satisfies 21 CFR Part 203.31(d) requirements for maintaining distribution records. The call unlock feature allows authorized users to reopen submitted calls for correction, with the unlock action itself recorded in the audit trail.
